newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-STEVE COPPELL APPOINTED MANCHESTER CITY MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STEVE COPPELL APPOINTED MANCHESTER CITY MANAGER.

text.p: Former Manchester United winger Steve Coppell was named as the new manager of first division Manchester City on Monday, ending the club's 42-day search for a sucessor to Alan Ball.

Coppell, 41, whose playing career with United and England was cut short by injury when he was 28, will travel north from his London home later on Monday to meet chairman Francis Lee and club officials.

Coppell has taken the job after resigning as technical director at Crystal Palace. Twelve days ago current Palace boss Dave Bassett, who replaced Coppell as manager at Selhurst Park, turned down the City job.
Coppell confirmed his appointment on Monday morning, saying: "It's a terrific challenge. I am delighted it's settled and I can get on with the task ahead of me.

"Manchester City have to be one of the best supported clubs in the country. I think it's only a matter of time before Manchester City are back in the premier league among the big names. They have wonderful fans and we might need just a little patience."
A succession of managers turned down the chance to revive the ailing club including Bassett, George Graham, Bruce Rioch, Howard Kendall and Willie Donachie.

Coppell won 42 caps for England. After starting his career at Tranmere he made over 300 appearances for Manchester United and later managed Crystal Palace whom he took to the 1990 Cup Final which they lost to United after a replay.
